sentences.en: all about constitutional principle and nothing at all to do with slavery.

sentences.zh: 白人南方人甚至在阿波马托克斯之前，实际上当然是在阿波马托克斯之后，就开始重写历史，声称战争与奴隶制无关。

sentences.en: But Adam, here's an interesting thing, though.
sentences.zh: 但亚当，这里有个有趣的地方。

sentences.en: So, in 1861, when they broke away, a moment we haven't talked about, the vice president
sentences.zh: 在1861年他们分裂时，我们还没谈到那个时刻，邦联的副总统

sentences.en: of the Confederacy, Alexander Stevens, gives this incredibly famous speech, this inflammatory speech, really.
sentences.zh: 亚历山大·斯蒂芬斯发表了那篇极其著名的演讲，那篇极具煽动性的演讲。

sentences.en: I think it's called a cornerstone speech, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我想它被称为“基石演说”，对吧？

sentences.en: Where he basically says, let's make no bones about it.
sentences.zh: 他在演讲中基本上说，让我们直言不讳吧。

sentences.en: Our state is founded on white supremacy, on the idea that white people are better than black people.
sentences.zh: 我们的国家建立在白人至上主义的基础上，建立在白人优于黑人的观念之上。

sentences.en: There always will be.
sentences.zh: 永远都会是这样。

sentences.en: There's an end to it.
sentences.zh: 这是有终点的。

sentences.en: So, white supremacy and slavery are right there in the Confederacy from the very beginning.
sentences.zh: 所以，白人至上主义和奴隶制从一开始就存在于邦联之中。

sentences.en: So, why is it?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么呢？

sentences.en: I mean, if they really believe in this,
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果他们真的相信这一点，

sentences.en: why is Jefferson Davis and why are other Southerners at the end of the war saying, oh, well, actually, no, it was just about states' rights in the Constitution?
sentences.zh: 为什么杰斐逊·戴维斯和其他南方人在战争结束时会说，哦，不，其实这只是关于宪法中的州权？

sentences.en: I mean, does that suggest that they had always secretly felt guilty about slavery?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这是否暗示他们一直对奴隶制感到暗自愧疚？

sentences.en: Why have they ditched the principle for which they had fought so quickly at the end of the war?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们在战争结束时如此迅速地抛弃了他们为之奋斗的原则？

sentences.en: I know slavery has been abolished, but why aren't they still saying it was a disgrace that you abolished slavery?
sentences.zh: 我知道奴隶制已经被废除了，但为什么他们不继续说废除奴隶制是一种耻辱呢？

sentences.en: Slavery was brilliant.
sentences.zh: 奴隶制很棒。

sentences.en: I mean, why are they not making that case?
sentences.zh: 我是说，为什么他们不那样辩解呢？

sentences.en: Well, some of them do make the case, not that it was a disgrace that you abolished slavery so much as wasn't it a sad thing, really?
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们中有些人确实那样辩解，与其说废除奴隶制是耻辱，不如说那真是一件令人悲伤的事情，不是吗？

sentences.en: You know, much in the way that in Chekhov plays, there's a kind of nostalgia for the days of serfdom.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像在契诃夫的戏剧中，人们对农奴制时代有一种怀旧之情。

sentences.en: This notion that, you know, actually, things were a lot more stable, and everybody knew where they were, and fundamentally, everybody was happier.
sentences.zh: 这种观念认为，你知道，实际上，当时的情况要稳定得多，每个人都知道自己的位置，从根本上说，每个人都更快乐。

sentences.en: So, there is that part of it.
sentences.zh: 所以，确实有这部分原因。

sentences.en: And I think that, you know, that continues long into the 20th, probably into the 21st century,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，你知道，这种感觉一直持续到20世纪，可能一直持续到21世纪，

sentences.en: this lingering sense that actually, maybe slavery really, you know, we would have been better if we'd kept it.
sentences.zh: 这种挥之不去的念头，即实际上，也许奴隶制真的，你知道，如果我们保留它会更好。

sentences.en: But it was alongside this kind of tacit acceptance that, well, you know, look, it's gone everywhere else in the world.
sentences.zh: 但这伴随着一种默许，即，好吧，你看，它在世界其他地方已经消失了。

sentences.en: And that this is not a hill anymore, on which it's possible to die, even if they wanted to.
sentences.zh: 这不再是一个值得为之牺牲的阵地，即使他们想这样做。

sentences.en: And of course, what they definitely don't do is to move away from their commitment to maintaining white home rule, or white supremacy in the southern states.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们绝对没有放弃的是他们对维持南方各州白人自治或白人至上主义的承诺。

sentences.en: In fact, they remain as committed to that as ever.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们对此依然坚定不移。

sentences.en: So, the line in the South in the immediate aftermath of the war is, okay, well, we will grudgingly, reluctantly accept that our bid for independence is over.
sentences.zh: 所以，南方在战后初期的立场是，好吧，我们会勉强、不情愿地接受我们争取独立的尝试已经结束。

sentences.en: And we will even, if we absolutely have to, accept that slavery in the form that had existed up until now looks like that's gone as well.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至会，如果必须的话，接受那种直到现在还存在的奴隶制形式似乎也已经结束了。

sentences.en: This has been a devastating experience for all of us.
sentences.zh: 这对我们所有人来说都是一次毁灭性的经历。

sentences.en: We've all lost thousands of dollars of property, including our property and human beings.
sentences.zh: 我们都损失了数千美元的财产，包括我们作为人类的财产。

sentences.en: But what we absolutely will not do is to knuckle under the yoke of the Yankee radical Jacobins who have now taken power in Washington.
sentences.zh: 但我们绝对不会做的是，屈服于现在在华盛顿掌权的激进雅各宾派北方佬的枷锁之下。

sentences.en: And so we will not cede our right to control racial affairs in the South.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不会放弃我们在南方控制种族事务的权利。

sentences.en: And on that, they do not yield and they win for generations.
sentences.zh: 在这一点上，他们没有让步，并且赢得了几代人的时间。

sentences.en: Okay, so we'll come to the implications of that in a minute.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们稍后再谈谈这带来的影响。

sentences.en: But you mentioned the radical Yankee
sentences.zh: 但你提到了华盛顿的激进北方佬

sentences.en: Jacobins in Washington.
sentences.zh: 雅各宾派。

sentences.en: And of course, there is one particular radical Jacobin Yankee in Washington, who dies almost immediately.

sentences.zh: 不幸的是它发生在剧院，但那是在1865年的耶稣受难日。

sentences.zh: 但你知道，我真的不知道最终会有什么不同。

sentences.zh: 我是说，我不禁觉得它确实有影响。

sentences.zh: 林肯拥有政治灵活性，懂得如何与国会合作，

sentences.zh: 白人南方人说，好吧，看，如果你想维持稳定，如果你想
